lead: The McCabe-Thiele method counts the theoretical stages of a binary distillation column on a y-x diagram. It replaces a column by a staircase between the equilibrium curve and two straight operating lines. The equilibrium curve comes from VLE; the operating lines come from reflux ratio and material balance. A feed line fixes where the two sections meet. Engineers use it for a quick tray count before rigorous simulation. It assumes constant molar overflow, so the operating lines are straight.
prereq: You need VLE and relative volatility, flash balances and simple distillation balances.

sections.h3: Rectifying line, stripping line and q-line

blocks.text: In the rectifying section above the feed, liquid L flows down and vapour V rises. The reflux ratio is R = L/D, where D is the distillate molar flow. Constant molar overflow keeps L and V constant in this section. A balance around the top gives the rectifying operating line.

blocks.where: y is vapour mole fraction of the more volatile component; x is liquid mole fraction; R = L/D is the reflux ratio; x_D is distillate mole fraction. The line passes through (x_D, x_D).

blocks.text: Below the feed, the stripping section has its own operating line. It passes through (x_B, x_B), where x_B is the bottoms mole fraction, and through the point where the rectifying line meets the feed line. A balance around the bottom gives it.

blocks.where: L′ and V′ are stripping-section liquid and vapour molar flows; B is bottoms molar flow; x_B is bottoms mole fraction.

blocks.text: q measures the thermal state of the feed. It is the heat needed to turn 1 mol of feed into saturated vapour, divided by the molar latent heat. For a feed between its bubble point and its dew point, q also equals the moles of liquid formed per mole of feed. The feed line, or q-line, is:

blocks.where: x_F is feed mole fraction; q is the feed thermal state defined above; the slope of the line is q/(q−1). The q-line passes through (x_F, x_F).

items: q = 1: saturated liquid, vertical line x = x_F.
q = 0: saturated vapour, horizontal line y = x_F.
0 < q < 1: two-phase feed, line slopes down from (x_F, x_F).
q > 1: subcooled liquid, slope q/(q−1) is positive and greater than 1.
q < 0: superheated vapour, slope q/(q−1) is positive and less than 1.

blocks.text: The q-line is not an operating line. It only locates the intersection P of the two operating lines.

sections.h3: Staircase between equilibrium and operating lines

blocks.text: Use a y-x diagram. The equilibrium curve for constant relative volatility α is:

blocks.where: y* is vapour mole fraction in equilibrium with liquid x; α is relative volatility; x is liquid mole fraction. Solved for x, this gives x* = y / [α − (α−1)y], the liquid in equilibrium with a vapour of composition y.

blocks.text: Draw the diagonal y = x. Mark x_D, x_F and x_B on it. Draw the rectifying line from (x_D, x_D) to the q-line. Draw the q-line through (x_F, x_F) with slope q/(q−1); for a saturated liquid feed this is the vertical line x = x_F. Its intersection with the rectifying line is P. Draw the stripping line from (x_B, x_B) through P.

items: Move horizontally left to the equilibrium curve. This gives x*, the liquid mole fraction in equilibrium with the vapour of composition y at that height.

Move vertically down to the operating line in use. Keep the rectifying line while x is above x_P, the x-coordinate of P. When a horizontal step takes x below x_P, switch to the stripping line. Only for a saturated liquid feed (q = 1) does x_P equal x_F.
Repeat horizontal to equilibrium, vertical to operating line.
Stop when x ≤ x_B. Each horizontal step to the equilibrium curve is one equilibrium contact; the vertical move only sets up the next step, and the final step may be horizontal alone.

blocks.text: The final step that crosses x_B includes the partial reboiler. Do not add the reboiler again. The number of real trays needed is greater than the theoretical stage count, because tray efficiency is below one (see tray efficiency).

sections.h3: Why the lines are straight; use and limits

blocks.text: Constant molar overflow assumes equal molar latent heats, negligible heat of mixing, and negligible sensible heat. One mole of vapour condensing then supplies one mole of liquid vaporising. L and V stay constant in each section, so the operating lines are straight.

The method gives the theoretical stage count at a chosen R. A lower R moves the operating lines closer to the equilibrium curve, so more stages are needed. At minimum reflux the steps never reach x_B (see reflux ratio). If CMO fails, use the enthalpy method (see Ponchon-Savarit).
The construction is used for binary columns, for checking rigorous simulation results, and for seeing how feed condition shifts the operating lines.

figure.caption: Construction for x_D = 0.95, x_B = 0.05, x_F = 0.40 and R = 2; the q-line is vertical at x_F. Notice that the operating lines meet on the q-line.

spec.aria: McCabe-Thiele construction on a y-x plot: equilibrium curve, rectifying line, stripping line and vertical q-line at x = 0.4.

examples.question: A binary distillation column separates a mixture with constant relative volatility α = 2.5. Feed is saturated liquid with x_F = 0.40, distillate x_D = 0.95 and bottoms x_B = 0.05 (all mole fractions of the more volatile component). Reflux ratio R = 2.0. (a) Write the rectifying operating line. (b) Find the feed intersection. (c) Write the stripping operating line. (d) Estimate the theoretical stages including the reboiler.
steps: Rectifying slope: R/(R+1) = 2/(2+1) = 0.6667. Intercept: x_D/(R+1) = 0.95/3 = 0.3167. Rectifying line: y = 0.6667x + 0.3167.
Saturated liquid feed means q = 1, so the q-line is vertical at x_F = 0.40. At this x the rectifying line gives y_F = 0.6667(0.40) + 0.3167 = 0.5833. Feed point P = (0.40, 0.5833).
Equilibrium vapour at x_F is y_F* = 2.5(0.40)/[1 + 1.5(0.40)] = 1.00/1.60 = 0.6250. P lies below the equilibrium curve, as it must.

Step from (0.95, 0.95). First horizontal: y = 0.95 gives x* = 0.95/[2.5 − 1.5(0.95)] = 0.8837. First vertical to rectifying line: y = 0.6667(0.8837) + 0.3167 = 0.9058. Continue, keeping the rectifying line until a step crosses the q-line at x = 0.40, then using the stripping line. The staircase crosses x_B = 0.05 after 13 equilibrium contacts.
examples.answer: Rectifying line y = 0.6667x + 0.3167; stripping line y = 1.5238x − 0.0262; about 13 theoretical stages including the reboiler.
examples.check:
alpha = 2.5
xF = 0.40
xD = 0.95
xB = 0.05
R = 2.0
rect_slope = R / (R + 1)
rect_int = xD / (R + 1)
y_feed = rect_slope * xF + rect_int
yF_eq = alpha * xF / (1 + (alpha - 1) * xF)
strip_slope = (y_feed - xB) / (xF - xB)
strip_int = xB - strip_slope * xB
def eq_x(y):
    return y / (alpha - (alpha - 1) * y)
x = xD
y = xD
stages = 0
while x > xB + 1e-12:
    x_eq = eq_x(y)
    if x_eq >= xF:
        y_op = rect_slope * x_eq + rect_int
    else:
        y_op = strip_slope * x_eq + strip_int
    stages += 1
    x = x_eq
    y = y_op
    if stages > 100:
        break
print(round(rect_slope, 4))
print(round(rect_int, 4))
print(round(y_feed, 4))
print(round(yF_eq, 4))
print(round(strip_slope, 4))
print(round(strip_int, 4))
print(stages)

traps: Stepping horizontally to the operating line instead of the equilibrium curve. The horizontal move gives the equilibrium liquid x* at the current vapour y; the vertical move gives the next operating-line y.
Counting the partial reboiler twice, or not counting it at all. The last step that crosses x_B includes one equilibrium stage for the reboiler.
Treating the q-line as an operating line. It only locates the feed intersection P; the operating lines are the rectifying and stripping lines.
Using x_D/(R+1) as the stripping-line intercept. That intercept belongs to the rectifying line; the stripping line passes through (x_B, x_B) and P.

Switching operating lines at x_F instead of at P. Keep the rectifying line until the horizontal step takes x below x_P, the x-coordinate of P where the two operating lines meet; then switch to the stripping line. Only when q = 1 is x_P equal to x_F.

quiz.q: In the McCabe-Thiele method, what does q represent?
quiz.a: q is the heat needed to turn 1 mol of feed into saturated vapour divided by the molar latent heat. For a feed between bubble point and dew point it also equals the moles of liquid formed per mole of feed.

quiz.q: Why is the q-line drawn through the point (x_F, x_F)?
quiz.a: The q-line is the locus of (x, y) pairs of passing streams that satisfy the balance around the feed stage. At the point where the streams have the feed composition itself, x = y = x_F, so every q-line, whatever the feed condition, passes through (x_F, x_F).

quiz.q: For x_D = 0.95 and R = 2.0, write the rectifying operating line.
A staircase crosses x_B after 13 horizontal steps. A student says the column has 13 theoretical stages without the reboiler. Correct the statement.
quiz.a: The 13 steps already include the last equilibrium contact at the bottom, which is the partial reboiler. The column has about 13 theoretical stages including the reboiler, not 14.

quiz.q: State the constant molar overflow assumptions.
quiz.a: Equal molar latent heats, negligible heat of mixing and negligible sensible heat; L and V are constant in each section.

quiz.q: What is the q-line for a saturated vapour feed with x_F = 0.40?
quiz.a: q = 0, so the q-line is horizontal at y = x_F = 0.40.

quiz.q: Why do the rectifying and stripping operating lines intersect on the q-line?
quiz.a: The feed is added at the feed stage. A balance around that stage must satisfy both section balances at the same feed composition and feed condition, so the two operating lines meet on the q-line.

beyond: Not for the exam. Process simulators solve rigorous stage models, but McCabe-Thiele remains a fast check for binary columns and a way to see why reflux and feed condition change the tray count. A spreadsheet can automate the staircase with the equilibrium expression and the two operating lines. Search next for 'McCabe-Thiele spreadsheet', 'constant molar overflow' and 'stage efficiency'.
